source.zone_name: Western Highlands Labor, Staple Crops, Vegetables, Trade and Remittances

source.zone_name: South Petén, Northern Transversal Strip (FTN) and Izabal Agro-industry and Food Crops

source.zone_name: Baja Verapaz and Quiché Staple Food and Agricultural Labor

source.zone_name: Motagua Valley, Fruit Agri-business Labor and Mining Labor

GT2016L108.notes: Land in ha as printed (better-off '>13' recorded as 13, lower bound). source.zone_name: Industrial, Agri-business Labor, Commerce and Services of Central Area

GT2016L109.notes: Land in ha as printed. Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p111); 'informal labor' (factory, transport, domestic, security, construction and agri-business casual work) plus 'female labor' (domestic service, prepared food) mapped to other_casual_labor - part of it is agri-business labour; 'wage labor' to formal_employment, 'business' to self_employment_trade. source.zone_name: Eastern Subsistence Food Crops and Agricultural Labor (Coffee, Fruit and Vegetables)

GT2016L110.notes: Land in ha as printed (better-off '>3.5' recorded as 3.5, lower bound); better-off cattle left null because the table says 0 while the text mentions cattle ranching. Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p120); 'casual labor' mapped to agricultural_labor (mostly local farm labour), poor 'domestic labor' to other_casual_labor, 'business' to self_employment_trade, 'wage labor' to formal_employment. Hazards and coping table continue on p122, beyond the segment's last page.

source.zone_name: Coffee Production

GT2016L111.notes: Five groups: the two 'middle' entries are lower middle (11%) then upper middle (5%); land is given in ha (midpoints; better-off 23-430 ha, cattle '>500' set to 500). Most shares read from Figures 4-5 (p129); 'agri-produce trade' (coffee trading / plantation cash crops) mapped to self_employment_trade, firewood/timber to natural_resources; better-off livestock 20% and trade 40% are stated (chart shows livestock ~25%). Poor staple self-sufficiency given as 2-3 months in one place and ~4 months in the calendar text; lean season Apr/May to mid-Aug, calendar Apr-Jul.

source.zone_name: Southern Agricultural Industry Labor and Food Crops

GT2016L112.notes: Land in ha as owned/cultivated plus rented (midpoints summed: middle 0.5-1 + 0.5 rented, better-off 1-2 + 7-10 rented). Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p140); 'labor sales' mapped to agricultural_labor, 'small business' to self_employment_trade, 'wage labor' plus middle 'female labor' (full-time service jobs) to formal_employment, poor 'female labor' (domestic service) to other_casual_labor. Irrigation is important for export plantations but most households lack it; lean season per calendar Jun-Jul (narrative: low labor demand May-Aug).

source.zone_name: Pacific Ocean Artisanal Fishing, Trade and Services

GT2016L113.notes: Table defines very poor/poor/middle (prose calls them poor/middle/better-off); middle land cell '> 0.7 0.08' is garbled so left null. Shares read from Figures 4-5 (p148); fish eaten (mostly in-kind payment for fishing labor for poorer groups) put under wild_food_fishing_hunting; 'local labor sales' (mainly fishing labor) -> other_casual_labor; fish sales -> natural_resources (text says ~half for poor and middle; chart shows ~40% for poor); 'female labor' -> self_employment_trade for very poor/poor (fish/craft selling) and formal_employment for middle (tourism wage labor). Other hazards: red tide, rough seas/warming water, resource over-exploitation, sugarcane expansion.

source.zone_name: Northwestern Pastoral Zone

KE2011L101.notes: Wealth table (rich/middle/poor/very poor) gives % of population and herds; a fifth 'sedentary' group (<5%, 8-15 shoats, no camels or cattle) is omitted. Only own-livestock food shares are given (better off ~60%, middle 'less than half', poorer 'less than 10%', recorded as upper bounds); no income or expenditure shares, and CFW enrollees meet half their food needs from aid. Months from the vector seasonal calendar (rains Mar-May and Oct-Dec; the text's 'short rains April-July, long rains October-November' conflicts); labour row is 'Labor Availability' peaks.

source.zone_name: Turkwell Riverine Zone

KE2011L102.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the average household (up to 5 cattle, 10-20 goats + 10-20 sheep, a camel). Income: food crops 'up to 40%' (upper bound); livestock 'about 25%' in one sentence and 'up to a third' in another, kept as 25-33%; firewood/charcoal and small business unquantified; no food shares. Irrigation judged high (maize and sorghum, ~80% of crops, are mainly irrigated); months from the vector seasonal calendar.

source.zone_name: Northwestern Agropastoral Zone

KE2011L103.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the typical household (5-10 cattle, 10-20 goats + 10-20 sheep, 'a camel/donkey' left null). Only quantified share: food and cash crop production 'up to 40%' of income (upper bound); firewood, charcoal, farm labour, petty trade, land leasing and gifts (poorer) unquantified. 'other' hazards = crop damage by wild animals and landslides; irrigation 'medium' because crops are both rainfed and irrigated; months from the vector seasonal calendar.

source.zone_name: Lake Turkana Fishing Zone

KE2011L104.notes: Food shares measured from the vector chart (axis 0.975 pt per %; stacks total ~96-98%, not 100%): fish -> wild_food_fishing_hunting (own catch), milk+meat -> own_livestock, aid+school feeding -> food_aid, social support -> gifts_other. Income only quantified for better-off livestock (18%); cash for work is the poor's main income but unquantified; expenditure 'two thirds on food' for all groups (no staple/non-staple split) left null. Rainfall 300-400 mm, reaching 1000 mm on the Marsabit side; harvest months are the calendar's 'Dry, Harvesting' season (Jul-Sep) though no crops are named; 'other' hazard = restricted dry-season grazing access.

source.zone_name: Northern Pastoral Zone

KE2011L105.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the typical household (5-10 cattle, 20-25 goats + 15-20 sheep, 0-5 camels); livestock 'up to 85%' of income recorded as an upper bound. Remittances and gifts 'up to 10%' of income for poorer households (not split, not recorded); most food purchased, meat/milk own-produced, wild foods used, but no food shares. 'other' hazard = restricted access to dry-season grazing; months from the vector seasonal calendar.

source.zone_name: Marsabit Marginal Mixed Farming Zone

KE2011L106.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the average household (up to 15 shoats, 10-15 cattle); income shares livestock 65% and crops ~30% (mostly khat/miraa, grown mainly by wealthier families); no food shares. Rainfall: zone average 500 mm (district 200-1000 mm); market access judged good (easy transport, food prices up to 70% lower and livestock prices up to 30% higher than pastoral areas). 'other' hazard = water scarcity, human_disease = HIV/AIDS; harvest months are maize from the vector calendar (teff harvested Jan and Jul).

source.zone_name: North-eastern Agropastoral Zone

KE2011L107.notes: Profile covers settled inhabitants; no wealth groups, 'all' is the average household (10-30 goats + 5-10 sheep, 10-20 camels, 5-15 cattle), income livestock ~60% and crops ~30%. Food described only within commodities (nearly all sorghum/millet, a third of pulses, two thirds of milk own-produced; rest purchased, much from Ethiopia), so food shares left null; casual labour, petty trade, charcoal and remittances unquantified. Calendar shows rains Mar-May and Oct-Dec while the text says April-May and October-November; irrigation 'low' (mainly rainfed, Ethiopian-highland floods used in Moyale); 'other' hazard = crop damage by wild animals.

source.zone_name: Mandera Riverine Zone

KE2011L108.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the average household (up to 15 shoats, 1-5 cattle, 1-2 camels). Own production 'up to 70%' of food (crops plus milk and fish; maize ~85% of crop food) is recorded under own_crops as an upper bound, purchases 'the rest'; income crops 'up to 60%' (bananas ~35% and onions 25% of crop income), livestock ~10%, petty trade, labour, firewood, fishing and remittances unquantified. Irrigation high (all crops but long-rains sorghum irrigated); livestock disease 'endemic' taken as chronic; months from the vector calendar.

source.zone_name: Northeastern Pastoral Zone

KE2011L109.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the average household (5-10 camels, 10-20 goats + 5-10 sheep, a few cattle); income livestock 60-80%, small business/petty trade 'up to 25%' (upper bound), sorghum sales and formal/casual labour minimal. 80-100% of cereals, pulses and vegetables are purchased (a within-commodity share, so food shares left null). 'other' hazards = restricted dry-season grazing and frequent water/pasture shortages (chronic, with endemic livestock disease); calendar rains Mar-May and Oct-Dec vs text April-May and October-November.

source.zone_name: Eastern Pastoral Zone

KE2011L110.notes: food_aid = relief ('almost half' poorer -> 45-50, 'a third' middle, 'a quarter' better off) plus school feeding 5-10% for all groups; purchase and own-livestock ranges stated. Income: middle/better off 'solely' from livestock (100%); poorer 'up to 40%' from animals (upper bound), the rest from self-employment (firewood, poles, gum: their main source), casual labour and zakat gifts, unquantified; herd sizes (20-30 cattle, 30-45 goats, 20-30 sheep, 0-12 camels) are for a 'typical household' and not assigned to groups. Rains from the calendar (gu Apr-May, deyr Oct-Dec; text says gu runs to June); 'other' chronic hazard = water shortages.

source.zone_name: Southeastern Pastoral Zone

KE2011L111.notes: No wealth groups: 'all' is the average household (20-40 cattle, 40-50 goats + 30-50 sheep, 0-5 camels); income livestock 'up to 70-80%', with charcoal/firewood, bush products, petty trade and casual labour for poorer households unquantified; food 80-100% purchased, and up to 80% of livestock products consumed are own-produced (within-commodity, not recorded). Rainfall 300 to 500-750 mm, up to 1100 mm in Lamu; calendar rains Mar-May and Oct-Dec (text: March-April and October-December). Irrigation 'low' (irrigation schemes help food availability); 'other' hazard = restricted dry-season grazing and unreliable water; endemic livestock disease taken as chronic.

source.zone_name: Coastal Medium Potential Farming Zone

KE2011L112.notes: Livelihood system set to mixed_other: despite the zone name, fishing is the main cash source ('up to 85%' of income, recorded under natural_resources as an upper bound), alongside farming, mangrove harvesting and tourism labour; livestock ~20% (mainly better off) and crops 10-20%; no wealth groups ('all' = typical household, 4-5 cattle, 5-8 goats + 0-2 sheep). Food mostly purchased; about half of maize and up to 40% of fish consumed are own-produced (within-commodity, not recorded). Rainfall given only per season (short rains 850-1200 mm, long rains up to 1400 mm) so annual left null; calendar rains Mar-May and Oct-Dec (text: long rains March-June); harvest = maize harvests (Jan, Jul-Aug, Dec); endemic livestock disease taken as chronic.

source.zone_name: Coastal Marginal Agricultural Mixed Farming Zone

KE2011L113.notes: No wealth breakdown: one 'all' group from zone-level statements. Food is 'mainly purchased' with own production (crops and livestock together) up to 50%, so purchase is recorded as >=50% (inferred); crop_sales 20% is cash crops only, and the text calls cash crops the major income source although livestock is 'about a third'. Livestock holdings are midpoints (1-3 cattle; 4-5 goats + 0-2 sheep); months read from the seasonal calendar; wildlife damage recorded as 'other' hazard.

source.zone_name: Tana Riverine Zone

KE2011L114.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group from zone-level statements (crops 'about half' of income, livestock 'up to a third'); food shares not given except that maize supplies up to 40% of food needs, so food_sources is null. Rainy months follow the calendar (long rains Mar-May, short rains Nov-Dec); the text instead says short rains Apr-Jul and long rains Oct-Nov. Agropastoral is a judgement call (riverine crops plus sizeable herds: ~5 cattle, 10-20 goats, 10-20 sheep).

source.zone_name: Southern Pastoral Zone

KE2011L115.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group (over 80% of food purchased; livestock 'over three quarters' of income). Rainfall is given only per season (long rains ~1,800mm, short rains ~500mm, implausible for a semi-arid zone), so annual rainfall is left null. 'Restricted access to dry season grazing' is recorded as 'other' hazard; endemic livestock diseases treated as chronic; holdings are midpoints of 10-20 cattle, 10-30 goats + 20-40 sheep.

source.zone_name: South-eastern Marginal Mixed Farming Zone

KE2011L116.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group with income shares from text (crops up to 40%, livestock 25-40%, remittances up to 10%; rest honey, casual labour, petty trade); no food shares. Rainfall given only per season (500mm short rains, 800mm long rains), so annual rainfall is null; short rains are the main cropping season (harvest Jan-Feb, green maize), long-rains harvest Aug. Mixed farming mapped to agricultural (judgement call); aflatoxin risk recorded as 'other' hazard.

source.zone_name: Southeastern Medium Potential Mixed Farming Zone

KE2011L117.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group (crop sales up to 40%, livestock about 40%, rest casual labour and petty trade). Maize is said to supply 'about 60%' of food and of cash income but it is unclear whether own-produced or of total, so food_sources is null. Months come from the calendar, which shows long rains Feb-May and short rains Aug-Sep (unlike neighbouring zones) and no lean-season row; about 20% of the population are out-migrant labourers.

source.zone_name: Southern Agropastoral Zone

KE2011L118.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group; own_livestock 'about a third' refers to sheep and goats only, and over two thirds of staples (not of all food) are purchased. Rainfall given only per season (1,800mm long, 500mm short), so annual rainfall is null; irrigation 'low' from the calendar note that horticulture is grown on irrigated plots. Crop damage by wild animals recorded as 'other' hazard.

source.zone_name: Central Highlands High Potential Zone

KE2011L119.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group; crop_sales sums cash crops (~30%) and food crops (~20%), livestock_sales is milk and poultry (~30%); poorer households rely on casual labour but no share is given. Own production (crops and livestock together) is about a third of food, the rest purchased. Holdings are midpoints (5-7 dairy cattle; 5-10 goats + 3-5 sheep); wildlife crop damage recorded as 'other'.

source.zone_name: Western Medium Potential Zone

KE2011L120.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group; petty trade, small business and casual labour together give about 20% of income and cannot be split. Own production (crops and livestock together) covers over two thirds of food, so purchase is recorded as at most a third (inferred). Rainy months follow the text (Mar-Nov with a July break); the calendar shows long rains Mar-May, short rains Aug-Sep and maize/bean harvests in Jun and Nov.

source.zone_name: Western High Potential Zone

KE2011L121.notes: No wealth breakdown and no income shares (crop sales first, livestock second); 'all' group only records that about a third of food is own-produced and the rest purchased. Livestock numbers are not given. The only cash figures are tea payments in the calendar footnote (Ksh 10.5/kg monthly, Ksh 24.6/kg October bonus).

source.zone_name: Western Lakeshore Marginal Mixed Farming Zone

KE2011L122.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group; crop_sales sums food crops (~30%) and cash crops (~15%); casual labour 'up to 10%' in cotton/sugarcane/tobacco areas mapped to agricultural_labor (judgement call). Rainy months follow the text (mid Feb-May, Jul-Oct); the calendar draws Mar-May and Aug-Sep. Market access is often disrupted in remote areas in peak rains (recorded as chronic market_disruption).

source.zone_name: Lake Victoria Fishing Zone

KE2011L123.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group; fishing gives 'nearly half' of income (natural_resources ~50, inferred), and crop plus livestock sales together about a third (not split); the rest is casual/formal labour, small business and remittances. Main harvest months are the sweet potato/cassava harvest from the calendar; drinking water shortage, lake pollution and low fish stocks recorded as 'other'. Holdings are midpoints (1-5 cattle; 2-10 goats + 3-5 sheep).

source.zone_name: Western Agropastoral Zone

KE2011L124.notes: No wealth breakdown: 'all' group; poorer households get up to 25% of food from wild foods in dry-season months (seasonal, not an annual share, so not recorded). Rainfall: zone mean 400mm, 250-500mm in drier parts and 750-1,250mm in mountains. Restricted dry-season grazing and drinking water shortage recorded as 'other' hazard; holdings are midpoints (5-10 cattle; 30-40 goats + 20-25 sheep).

source.zone_name: Central Karonga Livelihood Zone (CKA)

MW2016L101.notes: Wealth-group % of households measured from the vector bar chart (34/32/21/13; text: very poor+poor = 66%); food, expenditure and some income shares measured from raster charts (pixel-measured), stated values from text/MWK amounts otherwise. Text gives remittances as 17% and 15% for middle/better-off but the MWK amounts (46,400; 70,000) and chart give ~7%: amounts used. Middle 'ag. labor' chart segment (~5%) is off-farm brick labour per text -> other_casual_labor. Unmapped income: land rental (VP 4%, P 2%) and credit (middle 3%). Self-employment (baskets, mats, firewood) -> self_employment_trade; fish sales -> natural_resources. Land in acres converted x0.405 (table ranges, midpoints); cattle include oxen. Self-sufficiency: VP/P 3-4 months stated, middle/better-off cover the full year.

source.zone_name: Chitipa Maize and Millet Livelihood Zone (CHI)

MW2016L102.notes: Wealth-group % from the vector bar chart (20/50/20/10; text: very poor+poor = 70%). Food, expenditure and most income shares pixel-measured from raster charts; crop sales (41/49/48/58), petty trade (5/10/16/10), cash transfers (VP 6%) and VP staple expenditure (16%) stated. Chart petty trade for middle/better-off (13%/7%) conflicts with text (16%/10%): text used. Text MWK agricultural-labour amounts (20,070; 15,800) conflict with its own 13-16% and the chart: chart used. self_employment_trade = self-employment + petty trade (+ ox-cart hiring for upper groups); unmapped income: land rental (VP 4%, P 3%) and credit/loans (middle 14%, better-off 13%). Water expenditure = MWK200/yr over total income. Acres x0.405; middle/better-off self-sufficiency inferred from stated surplus.

source.zone_name: Kasungu-Lilongwe Plain Livelihood Zone (KAS)

MW2016L103.notes: Wealth-group % pixel-measured from the raster bar chart (31/35/20/14, mid-points of ranges). Food, income and expenditure shares pixel-measured from raster charts; text gives mostly cross-group ranges (e.g. labour ~35% for both poorer groups, tobacco <15% / 45-55%). Stated: VP inputs ~4%, non-staple food ~15% (poor) and ~12% (better-off; chart 16.5%/12%). Migrant labour (Zambia) is inside agricultural_labor; self-employment (bricks, firewood, baking) -> self_employment_trade; better-off credit (~14% of cash income) left unmapped. Acres x0.405; better-off cattle include 2 oxen; poorer groups' stocks run out by about October (~6 months).

source.zone_name: Phalombe Plain & Lake Chilwa (PHA)

MW2016L104.notes: All charts are raster images: shares measured from pixel heights (wealth bars normalised to sum ~100; food chart exceeds 100% for middle/better off); text values used where group-specific (VP payment in kind 16%, BO own crops ~80% vs chart 81%, poor non-staple spend ~25% vs chart 26%). Mappings: 'self employment' (VP firewood sales) -> natural_resources, petty trade -> self_employment_trade, egg+livestock sales -> livestock_sales, BO 'credit' -> transfers; land converted from acres (x0.405), BO cattle includes 0-2 oxen; staple months (6) inferred from stocks running out in October.

source.zone_name: Lower Shire Valley (LSH)

MW2016L105.notes: Most food and poorer-group income shares are stated in the text (VP/P food aid = 3% school feeding + 4% relief grain + 1% beans; construction labour = 51%/31% minus self-employment 32%/23%); middle/better-off food and income and most expenditure shares measured from raster charts (text says M/BO own crops '83 to 92%' and elsewhere '75 to 89%'; chart 75/88 used). Self-employment of VP (firewood) and P (quarry mining, fishing) -> natural_resources, M/BO (petty trade) -> self_employment_trade; livestock product sales included in livestock_sales; land from acres (x0.405), cattle include oxen, BO shoats include 0-5 sheep; staple months (6.5) inferred from 5-7 months of staple purchase; poor 47% and better off 10% stated, VP and middle measured from bar chart.

source.zone_name: Middle Shire (MSH)

MW2016L106.notes: Raster charts measured from pixels; text conflicts: VP/P crop sales stated 7%/13% (chart ~11%/~20%), M/BO inputs stated 17%/26% (chart ~14%/~19%) - stated values used. 'Labor sales' (mostly ganyu but also brick making, domestic work) -> agricultural_labor; 'self employment' (charcoal/firewood, plus brewing and sand mining for middle) -> natural_resources, petty trade -> self_employment_trade, chicken+livestock sales -> livestock_sales; own maize + other crops -> own_crops, maize + other purchase -> purchase. Land from acres (x0.405); VP 36% stated, other wealth shares measured; reference year Apr 2014-Mar 2015 (not 2013-14).

source.zone_name: Misuku Hills Livelihood Zone (MSK)

MW2016L107.notes: Wealth-group % stated as ranges; food, expenditure and self-employment/petty-trade income shares pixel-measured from raster charts (text gives only multi-group ranges, e.g. own crops 58-67% lower groups); purchases, crop and livestock sales (from MWK amounts; middle/better-off livestock MWK145,750/162,000 assigned by chart), labour income and inputs are stated. Labour income (23%/12%) includes non-farm brick/timber work but the chart shows only 'ag. labor', so all of it is under agricultural_labor; brewing and petty trade summed into self_employment_trade. Acres converted x0.405; cattle include oxen, shoats include sheep; rainy season taken from the seasonal-calendar text (Nov-Mar; zone description says Nov-Apr).

source.zone_name: Mzimba Self-Sufficient Livelihood Zone (MZS)

MW2016L108.notes: No text percentages for wealth groups: % of households pixel-measured from the raster bar in the wealth table (~34/33/20/13); food, income and expenditure shares pixel-measured from raster charts except stated values (very poor payment in kind 18%, agricultural labour ~30%/25% vs chart 31/23, livestock MWK6,000 and 147,500, non-staple food 17%/18%). 'Self employ' income mapped to natural_resources because the text says it is mainly firewood sales (petty trade shown separately -> self_employment_trade; better-off transport + small business -> self_employment_trade); construction -> other_casual_labor; milk/egg sales added to livestock_sales; tomato and tobacco sales added to crop_sales. Acres x0.405; cattle include oxen.

source.zone_name: Nkhata Bay Cassava Livelihood Zone (NKH)

MW2016L109.notes: % of households measured from the vector wealth bars (26/32/26/16; text: very poor+poor 58%); household sizes from the text (8/7/7/6; table gives 6-8, 6-8, 6-8, 5-7). Food, expenditure and most income shares pixel-measured from raster charts (text gives only multi-group ranges); stated: payment in kind 8%, food aid 2% (school feeding), crop sales from MWK amounts for poor/middle/better-off (very poor amount garbled in text). Unmapped income: land rental (VP ~6%, P ~6.5%) and credit (middle ~7%, better-off ~5%); milk sales added to livestock_sales; firewood and wild-food sales -> natural_resources; better-off 'food stocks' (~4%) -> gifts_other. Acres x0.405; 'other' hazards are strong winds and crop destruction by wild animals.

source.zone_name: Northern Karonga (NKA)
